label: late-original "m" input in long sequences starting a/k/s/w with an early 0
explanation: Very sparse feature that fires only at the end of the original phase (t=6..9, mostly orig_idx 7-8, L=8-9) or at the <DEL> step, and never in the copy phase. Input m accounts for about 64% of activation mass and <DEL> for 16%. It favours sequences whose first token is a, k, s or w (a alone carries 56% of mass) and that have a 0 digit early on (positions 1-3). More digits overall raises the firing rate. The strongest example (a k 0 0 a j d m) also fires on the neighbouring d, 2 and <DEL> steps. Even so, it fires on only about 1% of late-position m inputs, and the conjunction with first token and early 0 still reaches only about 16% precision and 39% mass recall on dev. So these conditions are tendencies rather than a full rule. It does not fire at t<6, on short sequences (L<=6) or during copying.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=a (+3.82), orig3=0 (+3.71), orig2=0 (+3.37), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=m (+2.44), phase=0 & in_tok=m (+2.44), orig0=s (+2.38). Lower it: phase=2 (-2.42), next_out=- (-1.99), orig7=- (-1.80), orig8=- (-1.41).
